body: The condition is inverted. `user != null` means conditional passkeys are only set up when a user is already in the context (re-authentication). On a normal first login, where `context.getUser() == null`, `fillContextForm` is no longer called, so the passkey/conditional-UI data (challenge, RP ID, etc.) is never added to the login form. That breaks regular passkey login, which is the main use case. The old code set this up exactly when the user was *not* selected. If the goal is to enable passkeys for both cases, drop the user check; don't require a non-null user.

This won't compile. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments, but the only method in `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. It should probably be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. Also note that, combined with the `user != null` check in that method, the username form will now always be shown on re-authentication whenever passkeys are enabled, even if the user has no passkey credential.

This overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator#shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but has no `@Override` annotation, so a future signature change would silently turn it into an unrelated method. Also, always returning false means that during re-authentication (user already known) `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED` is false and no `allowCredentials` are sent. The browser will then offer every discoverable passkey for the RP, not just the current user's. `action()` rejects a mismatch (`WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER`), but the user experience is poor. Consider scoping this to the known user when one is present.
